data.title: Trading Plan: Can Nifty 50 defend 25,800, Bank Nifty hold above 63,000 as consolidation continues?
data.description:
Markets are expected to witness further consolidation and are likely to trade within the wide range formed on Monday. However, the broader market structure remains positive, according to experts. The Nifty 50 may continue to trade within the broad range of 25,600–26,000 in the coming sessions, with a decisive breakout on either side likely to trigger a strong directional move. Within this range, 25,600 remains a crucial support level if the index slips below 25,800, followed by 25,500. On the upside, a decisive breakout above 26,000 could open the door for further gains towards the 26,300–26,400 zone. Meanwhile, Bank Nifty is expected to trade within a broader range of 62,500–65,200 in the coming sessions. In the near term, 63,000 is expected to act as an immediate support level, while the 64,000–64,500 zone could pose a resistance hurdle.

On November 26, the Nifty 50 gained 65 points, or 0.25 percent, to close at 25,885, while Bank Nifty declined 168 points, or 0.26 percent, to settle at 63,535. The broader market breadth on the NSE remained positive, with 1,825 stocks advancing against 1,471 declining.

Nifty Outlook and Strategy

Neel Parekh, Derivatives Research Analyst at Samco Securities

Nifty has remained rangebound following its extended rally during the November series. However, the index continues to sustain above its 40-hour moving average, keeping the short-term trend positive.

Momentum remains subdued, with the MACD flattening across both daily and hourly timeframes. A decisive breakout above 26,000 could trigger the next leg of the upmove. On the macro front, the outlook remains supportive, with weakness in Brent crude and US 10-year Treasury yields, along with rupee appreciation, providing favourable tailwinds for equities.

On the derivatives front (December 1, weekly expiry), the nearest Put base 25,500 and Call wall 26,000 were unchanged, keeping the range intact. Near the money (25,650–26,150 strikes), writing was balanced (Puts +98.9 lakh contracts, Calls +68.9 lakh contracts), which tends to keep the index in a range. PCR (all expiries) rose to 1.08 from 1.02 and India VIX eased 4.7 percent to 16.84; overall, the signals are mixed, so price needs to confirm the next move.

Key Resistance: 26,100, 26,300, 26,500

Key Support: 25,700, 25,500, 25,300

Strategy: Buy Nifty December Futures at CMP, targeting 26,500, with a stop-loss at 25,850.

Jay Purohit, Vice President – Research at Spark Capital PWM

Technically, the Nifty has been consolidating within a relatively narrow range of nearly 355 points over the last two trading sessions, indicating a temporary pause following the sharp upmove. A significant positive development on the positional front is the bullish crossover of the 50-day and 200-day EMA, commonly referred to as the Golden Crossover. This development reinforces the improving medium-term trend structure and is a constructive signal for positional investors.

However, the daily RSI oscillator has moved into overbought territory, indicating stretched short-term momentum. Consequently, the possibility of a minor corrective phase cannot be ruled out. Following a sharp rally of nearly 3,500 points within a month, some degree of price-wise or time-wise consolidation would be technically healthy and could help the market build a stronger foundation for its next leg of the uptrend.

At the current juncture, the overall market setup remains constructive, supported by positive sentiment, improving technical indicators and renewed institutional participation. Thus, the preferred strategy should be to remain aligned with the prevailing momentum rather than anticipate a trend reversal.

As long as the Nifty sustains above the crucial support zone of 25,000–25,100, any intermediate dip should be viewed as a potential buying opportunity. On the upside, the immediate resistance is placed in the 26,350–26,400 zone. A decisive and sustainable breakout above this hurdle could trigger the next leg of the rally, potentially opening the door towards the 27,000 mark.

Key Resistance: 26,000, 26,350

Key Support: 25,600, 25,340, 25,100

Strategy: Consider accumulating Nifty December Futures on dips towards the 25,500–25,600 zone, with an upside target of 26,350. Maintain a stop-loss at 25,300.

Bank Nifty - Outlook and Positioning

Neel Parekh, Derivatives Research Analyst at Samco Securities

Nifty Bank scaled a fresh all-time high of 65,193 during the November series before entering a consolidation phase. The broader trend remains positive, with the index sustaining above its 40-hour moving average, while the daily 20, 50 and 100 DEMA continue to trend upwards, reinforcing the bullish structure.

However, the MACD remains flat on lower timeframes, indicating subdued momentum. A sustained move above 64,000 could revive buying interest and pave the way for the next leg of the upmove.

On the derivatives front (December 29, Monthly expiry), the nearest Put base 63,000 and Call wall 64,000 were unchanged, keeping the range intact. Near the money (63,000–64,000 strikes), writing was balanced (Puts +2.0 lakh contracts, Calls +1.7 lakh contracts), which tends to keep the index in a range. PCR (all expiries) was steady at 0.89. Nifty Bank on the upside, 64,000 is the immediate hurdle and a sustained move above it could trigger short covering towards 65,000.

Key Resistance: 64,000, 65,000, 66,000

Key Support: 63,500, 62,000, 61,500

Strategy: Buy Nifty Bank December Futures above 64,000, targeting 65,000 with a stop-loss at 63,400.

Jay Purohit, Vice President – Research at Spark Capital PWM

BankNifty has been consolidating within a relatively narrow range of nearly 900 points over the last few trading sessions, accompanied by the formation of small-bodied candles, indicating a temporary pause in momentum. Prior to this consolidation, the banking index formed a large bearish candle on the daily chart on Monday. Subsequently, it has been forming an Inside Bar pattern for the second consecutive session, highlighting indecisiveness among market participants and a lack of directional conviction in the near term.

After a sharp rally of over 11,500 points in a month, some price-wise and time-wise consolidation is healthy for a sustainable uptrend. Importantly, Bank Nifty continues to hold above its previous all-time high of 61,765, keeping the broader bullish structure intact. However, the daily as well as weekly RSI oscillators are trading in overbought territory, suggesting that short-term momentum is stretched and intermittent profit-booking cannot be ruled out. The 61,500 level remains a crucial support. As long as Bank Nifty sustains above this level, dips should be considered buying opportunities.

While the standalone chart structure of Bank Nifty continues to remain positive, the Nifty-Bank Nifty ratio chart indicates a possibility of relative underperformance by the banking index compared to the Nifty in the coming week.

Key Resistance: 65,200, 67,000

Key Support: 61,500, 60,370

Strategy: Consider accumulating Bank Nifty December Futures on dips in the 63,000–63,300 zone, with an upside target of 65,200. Maintain a stop-loss at 62,400.

data.title: China's Industrial Profit Surged Despite Headwinds
data.description:
China's industrial profit surged in October despite mounting domestic headwinds, as robust global demand for its tech products continued to turbocharge exports.

Profits at China's major industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier in October, accelerating from the prior month's 14.4% growth, according to official data released Friday. During the first 10 months of the year, China's industrial profit jumped 16.0%.

Profit growth was powered by the electronics sector, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Rising demand for artificial-intelligence computing power drove sustained profit gains across related industries, including memory chips and peripheral manufacturing, said Yu Weining, a senior official at the bureau.

During the January-to-October period, profits in the electronics sector doubled from a year earlier, contributing roughly 10 percentage points to overall profit growth among major industrial firms and serving as a key driver of their rapid expansion, said Yu.

Rapid growth in the new-energy and AI sectors also fueled strong demand and higher prices for base metals such as copper and aluminum from January to October, pushing profits up 60.2% from a year earlier in nonferrous metal mining and 71.7% across the broader nonferrous metals industry.

Friday's upbeat data contrasted with earlier data showing the world's second-largest economy lost momentum across multiple fronts in October, underscoring its uneven growth. Surging exports have obscured sluggish consumer demand, declining investment and a protracted property downturn.

Economists at ANZ said China's robust exports have failed to pass through to domestic demand. "Weak domestic demand has exacerbated both domestic and global imbalances, while persistent disinflation has kept onshore yields structurally low." they told clients in a note Friday.

Write to Singapore editors at singaporeeditors@dowjones.com

data.title: Brambles Bull Seems Sanguine on U.S. Retailer Destocking — Market Talk
data.description: Brambles's bull at UBS doesn't sound concerned about the impact of U.S. retailers' destocking on the CHEP pallet operator. Analyst Andre Fromyhr acknowledges inventory data showing U.S. retailer stock intensity was slightly lower in the September quarter than a year earlier, and expects this to be a small headwind through the December half. However, he tells clients in a note that underlying consumption volume appears to be stable or even positive. UBS has a buy rating on the stock and a target price of 24.50 Australian dollars. Shares are up 0.6% at A$22.50. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: COMEX gold rises, silver gains over 2%; can the recovery hold
data.description:
Gold and silver prices recovered in global markets on Friday, November 27, after a sharp correction earlier this week, with buying at lower levels and short-covering helping the precious metals regain some ground.

On COMEX, gold was trading at around $3,584.90 per ounce, up 0.57% from its previous close, while silver gained 2.64% to $41.61 per ounce, according to the latest available futures quotes at 00:54 UTC.

Silver had slipped towards $38 an ounce earlier this week, while gold touched a low of around $3,444 an ounce.

The rebound follows a selloff triggered by stronger-than-expected US economic data, which reinforced expectations of tighter monetary policy. October core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation rose to 3.3%, while US third-quarter GDP growth was revised upwards to 4.3%.

Why are gold and silver prices recovering?

The recent recovery has been supported by bargain buying and short-covering after the sharp decline.

Prithviraj Kothari, Managing Director of RiddiSiddhi Bullions Ltd., President of the India Bullion and Jewellers Association and Chairman of Jain International Trade Organisation, said gold had fallen to around $3,426 an ounce, while silver declined to nearly $38 an ounce following stronger US economic data.

He attributed the subsequent recovery to bargain buying and safe-haven demand after the Trump administration proposed fresh tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China.

Saumil Gandhi, Senior Analyst – Commodities at HDFC Securities, said short-covering ahead of the US Thanksgiving holiday had also helped stabilise prices. When traders close bearish positions, they buy back the metal, providing temporary support to prices.

However, the recovery has not altered the broader monetary policy concerns facing bullion markets.

Strong dollar and rate expectations weigh on bullion

The US dollar is heading towards its third consecutive monthly gain, supported by safe-haven demand and expectations of further monetary tightening.

The dollar index was around 103.8 on Friday, up approximately 1.8% for November. Markets are pricing in a high probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Federal Reserve in December.

US Treasury yields also remained elevated, with the 10-year yield near 4.89% and the two-year yield around 4.67%.

Higher interest rates and bond yields generally reduce the attractiveness of gold and silver, which do not generate interest income. A stronger dollar also makes these metals more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

Vikram Kasat, Chief Business Officer – Advisory and Dealing at PL Capital, said movements in the dollar and crude oil, along with uncertainty around proposed US tariffs, remained important factors for financial markets.

He also flagged the rupee's weakness and Brent crude trading above $95.50 a barrel as potential pressures on India's import bill and inflation.

Silver's 67% correction: Is the metal nearing a turning point?

Silver's recent decline has been particularly steep. According to PL Capital, COMEX silver has fallen nearly 67% from its record high of around $121.60 an ounce on January 29.

The brokerage attributed the correction to expectations of further US rate hikes, selling in global equities that prompted investors to liquidate metal holdings to raise cash, and continued outflows from silver ETFs.

Its technical analysis suggests that the $37-39.50 an ounce range could act as an important support zone, where prices may consolidate and attempt to form a base.

PL Capital has identified $43 an ounce as the first level to watch for signs of recovery. A move beyond this could take silver towards $46-47 an ounce, followed by $51-52 an ounce.

The brokerage, however, cautioned against treating the recent rebound as a confirmed reversal. It said two consecutive weeks of positive closing prices, while holding the identified support zone, would provide stronger confirmation of a recovery.

What is happening to domestic gold and silver prices?

In the domestic market, gold prices recovered on Thursday, November 26, while silver remained unchanged.

Gold of 99.9% purity in New Delhi rose by ₹1,500 to ₹1.27 lakh per 10 grams, inclusive of all taxes, compared with ₹1.26 lakh in the previous session, according to local traders. Silver remained unchanged at ₹1.50 lakh per kg.

Gaurav Garg, Head of Research at brokerage platform Lemonn, said domestic gold prices recovered after the previous session's decline, with buying emerging at lower levels. He also pointed to the rupee's depreciation against the US dollar as a factor supporting domestic prices.

Jateen Trivedi, VP-Research Analyst, Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said gold pared some of its early gains as investors booked profits.

The World Gold Council's latest assessment has also pointed to resilience in Indian gold demand, with dip-buying, jewellery purchases and improving inflows into gold ETFs supporting the market despite the recent price correction.

What should investors watch next?

The Federal Reserve's December 8-9 policy meeting will be an important trigger for precious metals, alongside movements in the US dollar and Treasury yields.

data.title: Japan Inflation Likely to Accelerate on Energy, Food — Market Talk
data.description: Energy and food costs are expected to keep pushing up Japan's consumer prices, fueling inflation concerns and expectations for further monetary tightening. "In addition to rising energy costs and a diminishing downward drag from rice prices, continued cost pass-through--primarily in goods--will likely accelerate core consumer inflation further," says Daiwa Securities economist Kento Minami. data.title: India tribunal orders $52mn payout to Jet Airways staff
data.description:
India's National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has ordered that Jet Airways employees receive INR4.8bn (around $52mn) in gratuity, interest and provident fund dues within two weeks, The Hindu reported on November 26. The order closes a seven-year legal fight by staff of the defunct carrier.

The ruling settles who gets paid first from what remains of the airline. Under the order, money owed to workers stays outside the liquidation estate, so those claims do not compete with lenders' claims under the distribution rules of India's Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). State Bank of India (SBI) and other financial creditors had fought that outcome through the tribunal and the Supreme Court.

Gratuity payments will go straight into employees' bank accounts. Provident fund contributions will be credited to individual accounts through the provident fund office. A final copy of the order has not yet been released.

On June 30, 2026, the tribunal upheld a decision by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) instructing the airline's liquidator to pay provident fund and gratuity dues to workmen and other employees in full. In doing so, it rejected appeals by SBI and seven other financial creditors that wanted provident fund, gratuity and pension fund dues counted as part of the liquidation estate.

The banks had argued that such dues could be kept out of the estate only if provident fund and gratuity funds were in existence when liquidation began. They said this condition had not been met. The NCLAT did not accept that reasoning.

SBI took the matter to the Supreme Court, which threw out its plea on August 31. Because the money had still not been paid after those rulings, the tribunal issued the November 26 order to impose a firm 14-day deadline and to set out the payment method.

The liquidation proceedings cover claims from about 11,800 workmen as well as other employees.

Jet Airways flew its last commercial service on April 17, 2019, and then entered the corporate insolvency resolution process. In November 2024, the Supreme Court ordered the airline to be liquidated after finding that the winning bidder, the Jalan-Kalrock Consortium, had not carried out its resolution plan.

data.title: Japan short-term yields gain as inflation bolsters rate-hike bets
data.description:
By Rocky Swift

Short-term Japanese government bond (JGB) yields edged higher on Friday as signs of persistent inflation reinforced expectations of a rate hike next month, while investors speculated about possible changes to debt issuance.

  • The 2-year yield (JP2YTN=JBTC), the one most sensitive to Bank of Japan policy rates, rose 0.5 basis point to 1.745%, up for a second consecutive day. The yield on the 5-year JGB (JP5YTN=JBTC) was unchanged at 2.050%. Yields move inversely to bond prices

  • Annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, data showed on Friday

  • BOJ board member Naoki Tamura said that the central bank must respond swiftly to signs of an inflation overshoot, including by accelerating the pace of rate hikes. The BOJ in October held its policy rate at 1.25% and will decide at its December 17-18 meeting whether to raise rates

  • "It appears that hawkish policy board members are singing from the same hymn sheet even after the stock market sell-off," Kaoru Shoji, Japan rates strategist at SMBC Nikko Securities, said in a note

  • US Treasury markets were closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. Euro zone yields rose, with Germany's 10-year up about 5 bps to around 3.27%

  • A finance ministry official said at a meeting of JGB primary dealers on Thursday that Japan could boost issuance of shorter-maturity debt in fiscal 2027 if overall debt sales rise, with Treasury discount bills the most flexible instrument and said there was also room for increases in 2- and 5-year bonds

  • "If the primary dealer meeting fuels expectations of increased issuance not only of short-term but also of medium-term bonds, that could weigh on the medium-term zone," Takuya Onizawa, a bond strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities, said in a report

  • BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda is scheduled to speak in Nagoya on Monday

  • The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 1 bp to 2.625%

data.title: Japan's Nikkei extends weekly gain as investors scoop up battered AI shares
data.description:
By Rocky Swift

Japan's Nikkei share average rose on Friday, extending its weekly gain, as investors scooped up recently battered AI-related stocks and domestic-focused shares found buyers amid market volatility.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 climbed 0.83% to 57,976.69 in morning trade and was poised for a 2.7% advance for the week. The broader Topix gained 1.21% to 3,795.68.

Trading cues were slim, with US markets closed overnight for the Thanksgiving holiday. The Nikkei has firmed in recent days after plunging 7.7% last week, when concerns mounted over the cost of AI infrastructure and potential restrictions on international chip sales.

"Big moves are unlikely in Japan today with the US market closed," Monex Securities analyst Yoshitaka Araya said in a note.

"A slightly firmer start is expected, but the rebound will likely be limited because the Nikkei has been in a correction recently.”

On the domestic front, annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for a Bank of Japan interest rate hike as soon as next month.

Markets remained fragile after the Trump administration proposed country-specific tariffs on goods from 14 major trading partners.

Middle East tensions also escalated, with Yemen’s Houthis saying they had struck Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery and Iran saying mines had hit ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

"Share prices have remained firm recently, particularly in sectors other than AI-related ones, such as defensive sectors and domestic demand sectors," said Maki Sawada, an equities strategist at Nomura Securities.

"This is due to the fact that Japanese companies are expected to see increased profits in fiscal 2026."

Shares in Japan Tobacco climbed 4.27% following a report it was considering partnering on a takeover of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands .

Market breadth was overwhelmingly positive, with 179 of the Nikkei’s 225 constituents advancing and 43 declining.

The largest percentage gainers in the index were Socionext , up 7.75%, followed by Furukawa Electric , 7.65% higher, and Kioxia Holdings , which gained 7%.

The largest losers were Recruit Holdings , down 3.97%, followed by Dentsu Group , 2.75% lower, and Capcom , which lost 2.26%.

data.title: Indian shares set to open higher, eye fifth weekly gain as inflows boost momentum
data.description:
Indian shares are expected to open higher on Friday as they look to extend their winning run to a fifth straight week, with the unwinding of global AI trade driving a return of foreign flows into local stocks.

GIFT Nifty futures (GIFc1) were at 25,962 points, as of 7:51 a.m. IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index , which closed at 25,884.5 on Thursday.

The 50-stock index and the BSE Sensex are up 0.3% and 0.5%, respectively, so far this week, consolidating after a blistering surge of 14.2% and 14.8% over the last four weeks.

"The (Nifty 50's) ability to hold opening gains, particularly around the psychologically significant 26,000 mark, will be key to sustaining the near-term momentum," said Ponmudi R, CEO at Enrich Money.

Foreign investors, who have been driving the rally, net bought shares worth 58.43 billion rupees ($632.05 million) on Thursday, as per provisional data. They have already pumped in a record $15.48 billion so far this month.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) edged up 0.5% on the day, as it looked to end a bruising month on a steadier note.

The regional index is down 8.2% for the month, against the benchmark Nifty 50's 12.3% surge.

Brent crude futures hovered around $96 per barrel as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

data.title: Iron ore heads for third weekly loss on weak China demand
data.description:
Iron ore prices fell on Friday to their lowest in more than a week and were on track for a third straight weekly loss, as weakening demand in top consumer China and expectations of higher supply dampened investors sentiment.

The most-traded iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) slid 1.13% to 654 yuan ($98.20) a metric ton, as of 0155 GMT. It hit its weakest level since November 18 at 645.5 yuan earlier in the session.

The benchmark January iron ore (SZZFF7) on the Singapore Exchange declined 1.5% to $87.95 a ton, as of 0145 GMT, after earlier touching its lowest level since November 18 at $87.5.

For the week, Dalian iron ore has lost 0.3% so far and the Singapore benchmark is down 0.11%.

Hot metal output, a gauge of iron ore demand, continued to fall and portside stocks rose, adding pressure on iron ore prices, analysts at broker Everbright Futures said in a note.

Average daily hot metal output fell for a seventh straight week, dropping 1% from the previous week to an eight-month low of 2.27 million tons as of November 26, data from consultancy Mysteel showed. That compared with a 0.3% weekly decline in the previous period.

Expectations of higher supply also weighed on iron ore prices, as miners may ramp up shipments towards year-end to meet quarterly and annual targets.

"It's hard to see an obvious improvement in domestic demand in the medium term; global iron ore shipments may rise further," said analysts at broker Yongan Futures.

Other steelmaking ingredients gained ground, with coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! and coke (DCJcv1) rising 1.57% and 1.51%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange advanced. Rebar ticked up 0.29%, hot-rolled coil nudged up 0.09%, and stainless steel rose 1.47%.

($1 = 6.6597 Chinese yuan)

data.title: Urban Company shares in focus after starting pre-booking for Native residential ACs
data.description:
Shares of Urban Company Ltd. are in focus on Friday, November 27, after the firm started the pre-booking of residential air-conditions under its 'Native' brand.

The company said it had earlier intimated the exchanges on November 19 that its board had approved the addition of residential ACs to the product portfolio of its Native segment.

On Thursday, it informed the exchanges that it started the pre-booking of residential air-conditioners: Native Ultra and Native Ultra Air (with a built-in air purifier on select modes), on the same day, exclusively on the Urban Company app with assisted buying available. It added that the entire range will be announced at launch.

Urban Company said the Native AC, priced at ₹55,499 onwards, comes with a five-year unconditional warranty that covers gas refills and a 10-year compressor warranty.

It said that over the years, the company has handled over 18 million AC service and repair jobs. The work has given the firm a first-hand view of how, when and why ACs fail in Indian homes, it said.

The company said the key problem is that AC manufacturers focus on cost reduction to manage rising input costs. It said one in three ACs require a gas refill within five years. Also, efficiency tests are run at 35°C outdoor temperatures, while peak summer in most Indian cities crosses 42°C. Cooling capacity drops sharply as ambient temperature rises, it said.

The other features of the Native AC include:

  • Cooling performance: Brings room temperature to 24°C in 21 minutes.(even in peak summers)
  • Built-in HEPA H13 standalone air purifier: Available on select modes. It captures fine dust, pollen and smoke.
  • Smart features: An app with real-time gas level and energy tracking, a remote than senses the temperature where are sitting so the AC cools to your comfort and voice control, Urban Company added.

Urban Company co-founder and COO Varun Khaitan said the Native AC is designed to solve these problems at the source and the five-year unconditional warranty, including gas refills, is how it stands behind it. "Like our water purifiers, this launch reflects our philosophy of building products that are durable, thoughtfully designed, easy to use and smart," he said.

The move announced by Urban Company will also keep shares of incumbent AC manufacturers like Blue Star, Voltas, and others as well.

Shares of Urban Company ended the previous session 3.2% up at ₹170.15 apiece. The stock has risen 18.4% in the past month and 37.9% in the past six months.

data.title: India's Swara Baby Products seeks $347.5 million valuation in smaller IPO
data.description:
India's Swara Baby Products (SWAB.NS) has set a price band of 105 to 111 rupees per share for its initial public offering, seeking a valuation of up to 32.12 billion rupees ($347.45 million), a filing showed on Friday.

  • The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth 5 billion rupees and an offer for sale of shares worth up to 3 billion rupees by existing shareholders

  • The IPO opens for subscription from December 2 to December 4, while anchor investors will bid for shares on December 1

  • The IPO has been cut from 10 billion rupees in draft papers filed in July, with the offer for sale reduced from 5 billion rupees, the red herring prospectus showed

  • Parent Brainbees Solutions , which also operates baby products retailer FirstCry, will sell shares worth up to 1.5 billion rupees, the filing showed

  • Swara Baby is a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, including baby and adult diapers and sanitary napkins, and also sells diapers under its own brands Cuddles and Shields

  • Swara Baby's consolidated profit rose 18.5% to 955.9 million rupees in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, while revenue from operations climbed 23.4% to 11.64 billion rupees

  • JM Financial and Avendus Capital are the book-running lead managers for the issue

data.title: Japan futures set for weekly gain as oil stays firm
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Japanese rubber futures were steady and on track for a weekly gain on Friday, supported by oil prices hovering near this month's high, although soft tyre demand limited gains.

  • The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for May delivery , was little changed at 430.5 yen ($2.70) per kg as of 0200 GMT

  • The contract has gained 1.7% so far this week

  • The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery rose 260 yuan, or 1.4%, to 18,790 yuan ($2,821.45) per metric ton

  • The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 90 yuan, or 0.59%, to 15,370 yuan per metric ton

  • Brent crude futures hovered near this month's high on Friday as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region

  • Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil

  • Tyre makers may be digesting channel inventory without raising output, which suggests end-user demand is weaker than expected, analysts from broker Zijin Tianfeng Futures said in a note

  • The operating rate of China's all-steel tyre makers fell 2.38 percentage points to 53.83% in the week ended November 26, from 56.21% a week earlier, data from rubber information provider Qinrex showed

  • Affordability is likely to remain the principal constraint on mass-market vehicle demand in 2027, following modest growth in 2026, said Fitch Ratings in a report

  • Automobile sales could influence the intensity of automobile manufacturing, which involves using rubber-made tyres

  • The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 239.6 US cents per kg, up 1.1%

($1 = 159.2800 yen)

($1 = 6.6597 Chinese yuan)

data.title: Mercedes-Benz plans new China JV for local auto part supplies
data.description:
Mercedes-Benz plans to set up a new joint venture in Beijing to procure passenger vehicle components for supply to its manufacturing venture with BAIC Motor , according to a filing with China's market regulator on Friday.

Under the arrangement, Mercedes-Benz China will hold a 70% stake in the new company, while Beijing Benz, the German automaker's joint venture with BAIC, will own the remaining 30%, the filing showed. Both parties will jointly control the venture.

data.description: Coliwoo retains its bull at RHB Research thanks to its higher-than-expected total dividend for fiscal 2H despite profit missing expectations on lower revenue. data.title: Asian Markets Mostly Higher as Sentiment Stabilizes
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Asian markets were mostly higher Friday, tracking gains in U.S. stock futures as sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilized.

"U.S. markets were closed for Thanksgiving, leaving global markets to trade largely off the late recovery on Wall Street in Wednesday's session," said Westpac's Neha Sharma in an email.

Asian markets have also taken cues from stronger U.S. stock futures. E-mini Nasdaq futures were up 1.3%, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.0% and 0.7%, respectively.

South Korea's Kospi rose 1.65% and Japan's Nikkei Stock Average rose 0.7%. China's Shanghai Composite Index added 0.2% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.2% higher. However, Taiwan's Taiex bucked the trend to drop 0.3%.

The gains came even as Nvidia ordered its manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, after the U.S. escalated its push to keep the company's AI chips out of China's hands, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Oil prices were mixed after rallying overnight. Iran has stepped up its strikes targeting some of its Gulf neighbors and ships trying to get oil and natural gas out through the Strait of Hormuz. Most recently, an Iranian drone attack on Kuwait killed two Italians performing maintenance on antidrone equipment, authorities said.

Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthi militant group attacked Saudi Arabia's Jazan oil refinery on Thursday and killed one worker, the kingdom's Ministry of Energy said in a statement.

The attacks offset hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, ANZ Research analysts said in a note.

However, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week in the seven days through Nov. 20, while gasoline and distillate stockpiles also increased, according to the latest data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude-oil futures rose 2.1% to $85.41 a barrel, while front-month Brent was down 0.4% at $96.20 a barrel, according to ICE data.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: China's Industrial Profit Surged Despite Headwinds
data.description:
China's industrial profit surged in October despite mounting domestic headwinds, as robust global demand for its tech products continued to turbocharge exports.

Profits at China's major industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier in October, accelerating from the prior month's 14.4% growth, according to official data released Friday. During the first 10 months of the year, China's industrial profit jumped 16.0%.

Profit growth was powered by the electronics sector, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Rising demand for artificial-intelligence computing power drove sustained profit gains across related industries, including memory chips and peripheral manufacturing, said Yu Weining, a senior official at the bureau.

During the January-to-October period, profits in the electronics sector doubled from a year earlier, contributing roughly 10 percentage points to overall profit growth among major industrial firms and serving as a key driver of their rapid expansion, said Yu.

Rapid growth in the new-energy and AI sectors also fueled strong demand and higher prices for base metals such as copper and aluminum from January to October, pushing profits up 60.2% from a year earlier in nonferrous metal mining and 71.7% across the broader nonferrous metals industry.

Friday's upbeat data contrasted with earlier data showing the world's second-largest economy lost momentum across multiple fronts in October, underscoring its uneven growth. Surging exports have obscured sluggish consumer demand, declining investment and a protracted property downturn.

Economists at ANZ said China's robust exports have failed to pass through to domestic demand. "Weak domestic demand has exacerbated both domestic and global imbalances, while persistent disinflation has kept onshore yields structurally low." they told clients in a note Friday.

Write to Singapore editors at singaporeeditors@dowjones.com

data.title: Short-Term JGB Yields Rise on Elevated Tokyo Inflation Data — Market Talk
data.description: Short-term Japanese government bond yields are higher after elevated Tokyo inflation data boost expectations for the Bank of Japan's rate increases. Consumer prices, excluding fresh food, in the Tokyo metropolitan area climbed 2.9% in November from a year earlier, compared with a 2.6% rise in October, government data showed Friday. The BOJ policy board is scheduled to hold its final meeting of the year on Dec. 17-18. Investors are focusing on energy prices and their implications for the central bank's policymaking. The 2-year JGB yield is half a basis point higher at 1.745% while the 10-year yield is down 1 bp at 2.625%. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
